ai.description: *Gracixalus medogensis* is a small tree frog (SVL 24–27 mm) with a yellowish-brown dorsum and dark brown lateral markings. It is distinguished by a truncated snout and granular skin on the venter.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gracixalus medogensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged, triangular or V-shaped marking between the eyes, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Gracixalus medogensis* inhabits moist subtropical broadleaf forests in the eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Gracixalus medogensis* is primarily nocturnal, remaining active at night to forage for small insects among the vegetation of its humid forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gracixalus medogensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in water-filled tree holes or phytotelmata. Its reproductive mode is phytotelm-breeding.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gracixalus medogensis* is found in the Eastern Himalayas of Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically inhabiting montane forests at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Gracixalus medogensis* consists of a series of high-pitched, pulsed notes, typically heard emanating from dense vegetation in humid forest habitats.
